input.question: How is detector-resolution smearing implemented in LuminosityFit?

answer_points.text: Explain construction of the 2D smearing/convolution component.
Explain how PndLmdModelFactory composes it into the fit model.

A.answer:
In model/PndLmdModelFactory.cxx, when resolution_smearing_active is configured, PndLmdModelFactory::generate2DModel invokes generate2DSmearingModel to construct a PndLmdSmearingModel2D from simulation-derived resolution map data—populating RecoBinSmearingContributions with Monte Carlo coordinate bin centers and calculated smear weights—and wraps the current 2D model into a PndLmdSmearingConvolutionModel2D. [evidence.08873b527eb593d445b58bdf, evidence.fd8267293affa84d7e14da7f]
In model/PndLmdSmearingConvolutionModel2D.cxx, PndLmdSmearingConvolutionModel2D implements resolution smearing by generating a 2D model grid across threads; for each reconstructed bin, it queries smearing_model->getListOfContributors, evaluates the unsmeared model at each contributor's Monte Carlo coordinates, weights each evaluation by smear_weight, sums the contributions into model_grid, and serves these precalculated values via eval(). [evidence.c76b20774ae141162e1caf97]
In PndLmdModelFactory, resolution input data is supplied through setters like setResolutionMapData or setResolutions; generateModel evaluates the configuration property tree for fit_dimension == 2 and delegates to generate2DModel, which verifies resolution_smearing_active, builds the PndLmdSmearingModel2D via generate2DSmearingModel, wraps the base model into a PndLmdSmearingConvolutionModel2D, and calls current_model->init() before returning the resulting fit model. [evidence.08873b527eb593d445b58bdf, evidence.fd8267293affa84d7e14da7f]

In model/PndLmdSmearingConvolutionModel2D.cxx, PndLmdSmearingConvolutionModel2D implements resolution smearing by generating a 2D model grid across threads; for each reconstructed bin, it queries smearing_model->getListOfContributors, evaluates the unsmeared model at each contributor's Monte Carlo coordinates, weights each evaluation by smear_weight, sums the contributions into model_grid, and serves these precalculated values via eval().

In PndLmdModelFactory, resolution input data is supplied through setters like setResolutionMapData or setResolutions; generateModel evaluates the configuration property tree for fit_dimension == 2 and delegates to generate2DModel, which verifies resolution_smearing_active, builds the PndLmdSmearingModel2D via generate2DSmearingModel, wraps the base model into a PndLmdSmearingConvolutionModel2D, and calls current_model->init() before returning the resulting fit model.

B.answer:
In PndLmdModelFactory::generate2DModel, when the configuration option 'resolution_smearing_active' is enabled in model_opt_ptree, the factory creates a detector smearing component via generate2DSmearingModel and wraps the existing unsmeared fit model into a PndLmdSmearingConvolutionModel2D. [evidence.08873b527eb593d445b58bdf]
In PndLmdModelFactory::generate2DSmearingModel, simulation resolution data provided via setResolutionMapData (or setResolutions) is converted into reconstructed-bin contributor lists (an internal support type<RecoBinSmearingContributions>) storing Monte Carlo bin centers and normalized smear weights, which are injected into the constructed PndLmdSmearingModel2D. [evidence.08873b527eb593d445b58bdf, evidence.fd8267293affa84d7e14da7f]
Within PndLmdSmearingConvolutionModel2D, generateModelGrid2D uses multi-threading to evaluate the unsmeared model at each contributor MC coordinate, weights it by smear_weight, sums the contributions into a discrete 2D model_grid, and serves these precalculated values in eval. [evidence.c76b20774ae141162e1caf97]

In PndLmdModelFactory::generate2DSmearingModel, simulation resolution data provided via setResolutionMapData (or setResolutions) is converted into reconstructed-bin contributor lists (an internal support type<RecoBinSmearingContributions>) storing Monte Carlo bin centers and normalized smear weights, which are injected into the constructed PndLmdSmearingModel2D.

Within PndLmdSmearingConvolutionModel2D, generateModelGrid2D uses multi-threading to evaluate the unsmeared model at each contributor MC coordinate, weights it by smear_weight, sums the contributions into a discrete 2D model_grid, and serves these precalculated values in eval.

input.question: What is the theoretical purpose of the DPM elastic-scattering model?

answer_points.text: Relate the elastic differential cross section to luminosity extraction.

A.answer:
The theoretical purpose of the Dual Parton Model (DPM) elastic-scattering parameterization is to phenomenologically describe the hadronic amplitude of high-energy pbar-p elastic scattering across a wide range of four-momentum transfers |t|, capturing diffractive structures such as dips and secondary maxima where simple exponential parameterizations fail. [evidence.9b25e3c227798bc426619240, evidence.09e1e56c03a9c1741b55b69c, evidence.67f23bc6024df70e7eb06da3, evidence.9f50b0df9d3d7078f1ea1dc8]
In the context of PANDA luminosity determination, the DPM hadronic amplitude is combined with the Coulomb amplitude to form the full elastic differential cross-section model used to fit the measured angular distribution, allowing stable extraction of absolute luminosity as the normalization parameter across beam momenta where hadronic interactions become significant or dominant without relying on unstable free fit parameters. [evidence.9b25e3c227798bc426619240, evidence.09e1e56c03a9c1741b55b69c, evidence.4bfb7160f3c8158ba59d70f2]

In the context of PANDA luminosity determination, the DPM hadronic amplitude is combined with the Coulomb amplitude to form the full elastic differential cross-section model used to fit the measured angular distribution, allowing stable extraction of absolute luminosity as the normalization parameter across beam momenta where hadronic interactions become significant or dominant without relying on unstable free fit parameters.

LUMINOSITY DETERMINATION - THE LUMINOSITY FIT FRAMEWORK
This chapter presents the LuminosityFit software, which counts as major work effort of this thesis, and can be found on the github platform [ 107 ]. It is responsible for the determination of the luminosity with the highest possible precision from the reconstructed data of the LMD. Recalling chapter 3 , this is achieved by comparing the measured elastic scattering angular distribution with the theoretical model distribution. The normalization variable is the absolute luminosity L . However the measured angular distribution N ( θ ) cannot simply be compared to the theoretical model σ ( θ ) , because several inevitable measurement effects alter the original pure elastic scattering distribution. There are two possible paths to overcome this obstacle. One possibility is to correct the measured data for the effects introduced by the ¯ PANDA spectrometer, which then allows a direct comparison with the pure elastic scattering model. Alternatively, the pure model can be modified to include all of the effects that arise during the measurement, so that is directly comparable with the data. The first option is in practice not feasible as required operations such as deconvolutions, which undo the detector resolution of the data, require very large amounts of data and a constant resolution to work reliably. On these grounds the second option was chosen, allowing for far more flexibility, extraction power and precision. The construction of the fit model with all of the transformations and correction procedures of the elastic scattering cross section is presented in detail in the following. Results on the extracted luminosity precision and studies of systematic uncertainties are presented in the next chapter.
4 . 1 the elastic scattering model
The cross section for elastic ¯ pp scattering was introduced in section 3 . 3 . Apart from the calculable coulomb part of the total elastic cross section, two possible parameterizations for the description of the hadronic part exist. Both parameterizations are implemented in the LuminosityFit software. Despite the fact that the E 760 parameterization is more suitable, because it uses more measurements in the four momentum range of the LMD, the DPM parameterization was chosen for the studies in this thesis (see equation 18 ). The reasoning is that the DPM generator is the only official generator for the ¯ PANDA experiment that includes elastic ¯ pp processes 1 . Moreover the operability of the LuminosityFit software and the validity of its extraction precision and studies on systematic uncertainties are not influenced by the chosen parameterization, as long as the behavior of the true physics cross section is described approximated. To ensure meaningful results of the systematic effects, the parameterization of the event generator and the fit model of the luminosity extraction software are identical.
1 The official version of the DPM generator unfortunately uses 32 bit floating point precision. For the small excerpt of the angular spectrum of the LMD, the numerical precision was not good enough. Therefore a special 64 bit precision version of this generator is used in the simulation studies

To overcome the severe limitations of simple analytical parameterizations, the Dual Parton Model (DPM) is employed as a robust phenomenological framework to describe high-energy ¯ 𝑝𝑝 elastic scattering [124, 125]. For the specific purpose of luminosity determination at PANDA, the primary practical advantage of the DPM lies in its ability to accurately model the hadronic amplitude across a wide range of momentum transfers ( | 𝑡 | ) without relying on unstable free parameters. Simple exponential parameterizations of the hadronic amplitude (e.g., 𝑒 -𝑏 | 𝑡 | ) via Eq. 3.6 are valid only at small momentum transfers [126, 127]. They completely fail to describe the complex diffractive structures, such as pronounced dips and secondary maxima, that inherently appear at larger | 𝑡 | values in ¯ 𝑝𝑝 scattering. Furthermore, attempting to extract the luminosity by treating fundamental variables like 𝜎 𝑡𝑜𝑡 , 𝑏 , and 𝜌 as independent free parameters for every single energy scan point can easily lead to unphysical mathematical fluctuations in the fit results. To overcome these experimental and phenomenological limitations, a more complicated DPM-based model is employed [128]:

The raw data acquired by the Luminosity Detector consists of digitized pixel hits distributed across four detector planes. The reconstruction chain is fully implemented within the PandaRoot framework as discussed before. The procedure consists of four sequential stages: Digitization and Hit Reconstruction, Track Finding, Track Fitting, Track Filtering and Back-Propagation, as illustrated in Figure 3.5.

The LMD detects antiprotons scattered at very small angles (3 -9 mrad). Using Eqs. 3.9 and 3.10, the corresponding momentum transfer | 𝑡 | can be calculated, as shown in Figure 3.3. Unfortunately, | 𝑡 | is not always at very small values where the Coulomb term dominates. At the beam momentum of 3 . 5 GeV /𝑐 , the hadronic term begins to take great effects, while at 12 GeV /𝑐 , the hadronic term dominates. Therefore, the full expression of Eq. 3.8 must be used to fit the measured differential cross section to extract the luminosity.

Installation of PandaRoot for Developers
========================================

# PandaRoot

This software is designed to the specific needs of the PANDA experiment. It is used to perform event generation, particle transport ("simulation"), detector digitisation and reconstruction, particle identification as well as event analysis.


### Installation
For **user installation** instructions please refer to [docs/Installation/Install_PandaRoot.md](docs/Installation/Install_PandaRoot.md)

If you do **development**, please follow the instructions in [docs/Installation/Install_Developers.md](docs/Installation/Install_Developers.md)

The installation at the **GSI cluster** Virgo is described in [docs/Installation/Install_GSI.md](docs/Installation/Install_GSI.md)

### Examples
To run a simulation chain with PandaRoot you can refer to `macro/master` which contains the most recent macros. More detailed examples and tutorials are found under `tutorials`. The most recent one is `tutorials/thailand2017`.

### Overview

There are many event generators, which can be found in `pgenerators`. The detector code is put at `detectors`. Under `geometry` the root geometries and related files are stored. 
The input and the parameters are located in `config`, `gconfig`, `input` and `macro/params`. Tracking and PID code is located in `tracking`, `genfit`, `genfit2` and `pid`. 
The analysis related classes are found in `analysis`. 
All data formats are separated from the actual algorithms and can be referenced in `pnddata`.

Under `macro/QA` you will find the quality assurance checks, which are performed each night. Their results can be found at [https://cdash.gsi.de/index.php?project=PandaRoot](https://cdash.gsi.de/index.php?project=PandaRoot).

export SIMPATH=/home/pandauser/fairsoft_XXX/install
  mkdir build
  cd build
  cmake -DCMAKE_INSTALL_PREFIX=../install ../source
  make install -j4

First you need to set the environment variables SIMPATH and FAIRROOTPATH, which are the folders where you have the installed the external packages and FairRoot. If the installation was done with Spack, both folders may be the same. On a cluster this may be already pre-installed for you, e.g. on a CVMFS.
